FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Continuous Bulk Conveying, Elevating Hoisting, Aerial Ropeways and Related Equipment Sectional Committee 
had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 


This standard was first published in 1994. Keeping in the view the latest technical changes. The Committee 
decided to revise this standard. In this revision the following important changes have been incorporated: 


a) Belt width, capacity and power rating of belt feeder modified. 
b) Parameters for vibrator feeders modified. 


Feeders constitute an important component in the material handling and conveying system involved in industrial 
units such as thermal power plant, stockyards, coal mines, fertilizer industry and chemical industry. They play a 
vital role in the operation of the plant as any operational problem relating to feeders can hamper the operation, 
growth and economy of industrial unit. This standard has therefore been brought out to the industrial units and 
manufacturers, designers and consultants to assist them in proper selection of the type of feeders to be used for a 
specific application. This standard is one of the series of standards being brought out on the selection of various 
types of feeders (see 4). The other standards in this series are: 


IS No. Title 
12060 : 1987 Code of practice for selection of rotary vane feeders 
12108 : 1987 Code of practice for selection of rotary table feeders 
12204 : 1987 Code of practice for selection of reciprocating feeders 
12215 : 1987 Code of practice for selection of belt feeders 
12400 : 1988 Code of practice for selection of electromagnetic feeders 
12401 : 1988 Code of practice for selection of mechanical vibrating feeders 


Types of feeders, for which no Indian Standards have yet been formulated to guide the industry for their selection, 
shall be covered in due course of time. 


The Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given at Annex A. 


For the purpose of deciding whether particular requirement of this standard is compiled with, the final value 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical value (revised)’. The number of significant places in the rounded off value 
should be the same as that of the specified value in the standard. 


IS 14169 : 2013 


Indian Standard 


RECOMMENDATIONS FOR TYPE 
SELECTION OF FEEDERS 


( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard lays down brief description for 
application of various feeders and guidelines for 
selection of such feeders for handling solid bulk 
materials. 

NOTE — Most commonly used feeders in various industries 


are belt, apron, screw, vibratory, reciprocating, rotary valve, 
rotary table and rotary plough feeders. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contains provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below: 


IS No. Title 

12108 : 1987 Code of practice for selection of 
rotary table feeders 

12204 : 1987 Code of practice for selection of 
reciprocating feeders 

12215 : 1987 Code of practice for selection of belt 
feeders 

12400 : 1988 Code of practice for selection of 
electromagnetic feeders 

12401 : 1988 Code of practice for selection of 
mechanical vibrating feeders 

12960 : 1990 Determination of power 
requirements of screw feeders — 
General requirements 

13324 : 1992 Screw feeders — General 
requirements 


3 CHARACTERISTIC OF FEEDERS 


Feeder is a device mounted at the outlet of storage units 
such as bins, bunkers, silos or hoppers to control the 
flow of material at a constant or variable rate. 


4 TYPES OF FEEDERS 


4.1 Belt Feeders 


4.1.1 Belt feeders may be horizontal or inclined or 
troughed flat. Belt speed is kept low. Belt feeders 
selected in accordance with IS 12215 generally have 


the following parameters: 


Belt width 400 — 2 000 mm 
Belt speed 0.1 — 1.2 m/s 
Capacity Up to 500 t/h 
Length 2-10m 

Power rating Up to 55 kW 
Lump size Up to 300 mm 


4.1.1.1 Inclination shall be taken into consideration 
while deciding the belt speed. 


4.1.2 Application 


Belt feeders are commonly used to convey ores, coal 
or concentrates and occasionally are used to convey 
very fine dry powders. They can handle practically any 
material which is not large, hot or sticky. The 
advantages and disadvantages of using belt feeders are 
as follows: 


Advantages 


Disadvantages 


Simple construction 


Positive extraction of 
material 


Good feed regulation 


Low power consumption 
Automatic control 
Low cost 


Can bear loading of 
material directly at feed 
point 

Less dust nuisance 


More space requirement 


Not suited to hot, very 
abrasive, lumpy and 
sticky material 


Fine powders which tend 
to flood can cause 
problems 


4.2 Apron Feeders 


4.2.1 Apron feeders may be horizontal or inclined. The 
angle of inclination in case of apron feeder can be larger 
than that of a belt feeder. Apron feeder generally has 
the following parameters: 


Width Up to 3 600 mm 
Length Up to 10m 
Maximum Lump size up to 1 500 mm 


IS 14169 : 2013 


Speed 0.05 — 0.5 m/s 
Capacity Up to 4 000 t/h 
Power rating Up to 110 kW 


4.2.1.1 Inclination shall be taken into consideration 
while deciding the feeder speed. 


4.2.2 Application 


Apron feeders are predominantly used for handling 
heavy, large lumped and also for medium lumped 
materials. They can be used to handle stone, ores, 
gravel, sand, coal and other sharp, abrasive and hot 
materials. They are recommended for installation 
where material falls from a distance causing impact. 
The advantages and disadvantages of using apron 
feeders are as follows: 


Advantages Disadvantages 


Large capacity More spares requirement. 
Requires lubrication 


system 
High initial cost. Not 
suitable for powdered 
material 


Positive feed extraction 
and uniform flow 


Convey up hill High maintenance 


Reliable with difficult loads High power consumption 


Can handle large lumped, Requires bed of fine 
abrasive, sharp and hot material on the pans to be 
material used under severe impact 

conditions

conveyor in some cases 
to collect fines falling 
through pan falling 
through pan interfaces 
Convey up to longer — 

distance 
Can sustain heavy bin — 

pressure 


4.3 Screw Feeders 


4.3.1 A screw feeder is essentially designed for very 
low outputs. It may be horizontal or installed at a slight 
angle. A flow control valve regulates the capacity or 
dyno drive is used to control the capacity of the screw 
feeder. A multiple screw feeder may be added where 
material has tendency to pack under pressure. Screw 
feeders generally have the following parameters: 


Length Up to 6.0 m 
Diameter Up to 360 mm 
Capacity Up to 60 t/h 


Screw speed See IS 13324 


Power rating : Up to 22 kW when calculated in 


accordance with IS 12960 
4.3.2 Application 


Screw feeders are used for powdered, granular and 
small lumped materials that are not affected by 
crushing. It is not recommended for highly abrasive, 
highly aerated fines and highly sticky materials. The 
advantages and disadvantages of using screw feeders 
are as follows: 


Advantages Disadvantages 


Provides dust tight 
enclosure 


Limited capacity 


Low head room 
requirement 


Cannot handle large 
lumped and abrasive 
material 
Assures positive movement Not recommended for 
of material highly sticky materials 
Comparatively low power — 
requirement 
Low maintenance cost — 
Ability to handle wide — 
range of solids 


4.4 Vibratory Feeder 
4.4.1 Two types of vibratory feeders generally used are: 


a) Electro-mechanical; and 
b) Electro-magnetic. 


4.4.2 Electro-mechanical vibratory feeder is driven by 
electric motor with eccentric weights operating at a 
frequency of 1 500 cycles/min with 50 c/s as line 
frequency. Electromagnetic vibrator feeder is driven 
by electromagnet. Their selection is generally guided 
by IS 12401 and IS 12400 respectively. They generally 
have the following parameters: 


Parameter Electro- Electro- 
Mechanical Magnetic 
Feeder Feeder 

Line frequency 50 c/s 50 c/s 

Frequency of 750 -1 500 3 000 cycles ppm 
vibration cycles ppm 

Amplitude of 3- 12.5 mm 1-2 mm 
vibration 

Drive angle 30° — 60° — 

Pan inclination Up to 10° Up to 10° 

Pan width Up to 2 500 mm Up to 2 000 mm 

Trough length Up to 8 000 mm Up to 4 000 mm 

Capacity Up to 3 000 t/h Up to 1 000 t/h 

Lump size Up to 1 500 mm Up to 200 mm 


Power rating Up to 75 kW Up to 15kW 


Feeding Generally Generally 
constant controlled 
Type Troughed/ Troughed/ 
tubular tubular 
Mounting Suspended/ Troughed/ 
semi-suspended tubular 
4.4.3 Application 


Vibratory feeders are used for coarse, medium, fine and 
concentrated materials. Coal, iron ore, lime stone, rock, 
coke, scrap steel and other similar materials may also be 
handled by vibratory feeder. Dusting problems arises 
with dry powdered materials. The advantages and 
disadvantages of using vibratory feeders are as follows: 


Advantages Disadvantages 


Feed extraction is not 
Positive 


Simple construction 


High capacity Very fine and sticky material 
may cause problems 


Automated control Dusting problem dry 


powdered materials 
Efficient material — 
transportation 
No spillage — 
Uniform flow — 


Shock absorbing — 
suspension 

Offers possibility of — 
scalping 

Low maintenance — 

No lubrication required — 


Very low power — 
consumption 


Low initial cost — 
Low installation cost — 
Low noise operation — 


4.5 Reciprocating Plate Feeders 


4.5.1 Apart from handling lumps, reciprocating plate 
feeders also handle fines which do not get packed in the 
hopper opening. Reciprocating feeders operate 
horizontally or at slight declinations. Reciprocating 
feeders are generally selected in accordance with 
IS 12204. They generally have the following parameters: 


Pan width : 315-2 000 mm 
Stroke length : 100-450 mm 
Strokes /min : 20-60 


Maximum lump size : Up to 1 200 mm 
: Up to 1 000 t/h 


: Up to 40 kW 


Capacity 
Power rating 


IS 14169 : 2013 


4.5.2 Application 


The plate feeders are most commonly used for 
discharging fine and medium materials. They are used 
under track hoppers and bins to handle stone, ores, 
coal and other non-sticky materials. Due to their simple 
construction and low cost, they are widely used in coal 
mining industry. The advantages and disadvantages of 
using reciprocating plate feeders are as follows: 


Advantages Disadvantages 


Simple construction High wear and tear 

Low initial cost 

Capability to handle 
all types of materials 


and lumps 


High maintenance cost 
Intermittent discharge 


Not suitable for sticky — 
material 


Speed adjustment — 


4.6 Rotary Valve (Air Lock) Feeders 


4.6.1 The rotary valve feeders are completely enclosed 
and present powders or fine grained material from 
flooding. These feeders can control discharge rates of 
fine or granular free flowing, dry solid materials. These 
feeders are used for flow rate up to 300 m*/h with a 
maximum lump size of 30 mm. 


4.6.2 Application 


Valve feeders are normally installed underneath 
hopper/cyclone outlet and provide air lock. It can 
directly discharge into a pneumatic conveying line. 


4.7 Rotary Table Feeders 


Rotary table feeders (see IS 12108) are suitable for 
sticky materials such as wet ore fines and low feed 
rates. It can accommodate hopper openings up to 
2.5 mm in diameter. They can handle materials which 
have tendency to arch. They are simple in construction 
and require very little maintenance. These feeders are 
used for flow rate up to 350 m*/h with a maximum 
lump size of 30 mm. Their disadvantages include high 
installation cost. In case of breakdown, recovery time 
is more. This is mainly due to series equipment parts 
are required for dismantling. For example repair of gear 
box requires complete dismantling of table. Hence 
more time is taken for recovery of equipment. 


4.8 Rotary Plough (Paddle) Feeders 


4.8.1 Rotary plough feeder has a wide field of 
application for materials like lignite, coal, potash, 
sinter, phosphate, lime stone, ore, cement clinker, etc. 
Rotary plough feeders are suitable for use in funnels, 
under storage pipes, under long storage bins or under 


IS 14169 : 2013 


slotted hoppers. In slotted hoppers, the bulk materials 
form a layer on a cantilevered longitudinal shell. 
Rotary plough (paddle) mounted on self-propelled 
carriage and rotating on a motor driven vertical shaft 
force off the material from the shell and discharges 
into another belt conveyor. The paddle wheel travels 
slowly along the hopper and unloads it uniformly, 
reversing direction automatically when it reaches the 
end of the slot. Rotary paddle feeder is becoming more 
and more popular for unloading track hoppers. It is 
used for high capacity that is, up to 2 500 t/h. It has 
high initial cost. 


4.8.2 Plough feeders are available in following designs: 
a) Single plough with single reclaim shelf for 
low capacity. 
b) Single plough with double reclaims shelves 
for high capacity. 


4.8.2.1 In both the types defined in 4.8.2 (a) and 4.8.2 (b), 
the drive system can be either above or below the shelf. 


4.8.3 The elimination of multiple feeders with multiple 
loading points on reclaim belt also reduces continuous 
skirt boards and material spillage. 


4.8.4 The advantages and disadvantages of using rotary 
plough feeders are as follows: 


Advantages Disadvantages 


First-in-first-out system 
eliminates the danger 
of spontaneous combustion 
when handling materials 
such as coal 


Higher initial cost 


Fully live storage — 


Suitable for all types of — 
bulk solids 

Suitable for handling even — 
cohesive solids 

Eliminates bridging and rat — 
holing due to long slot 
opening which is 
experienced with other 
types of feeders variable 
feed control 


5 SELECTION OF TYPE OF FEEDERS 


5.1 The type and size of feeder for an application 
depends on capacity requirement and characteristics 
of the material to be handled. Installation details and 
few other factors also play important role in selection 
of feeders. 


5.2 The factors which shall be considered for selecting 
a feeder for required application are listed below: 


a) Material characteristics: 

1) Material; 
2) Feed-rate, maximum and minimum; 
3) Bulk density; 
4) Maximum lump size; 
5) Size analysis; 
6) Moisture content; 
7) Angle of repose; 
8) Cohesiveness; 
9) Temperature; 

10) Flowability; and 


11) Any other property that may affect the 
selection. 


b) Installation and application details 
1) Hopper details: 
i) Surge hopper; 
ii) Overground/underground bunker; 
iii) Open stockpile; and 
iv) Dumper unloading hopper, etc. 
2) Process following the feeder: 
i 


Nar 


Belt conveyor; 
ii) Crusher; 
ili) Screen; 
iv) Loading into trucks/rails/others; 
v) Accuracy of flow regulation; 
vi) Control equipment for the process; 
vii) Maintenance requirements; and 
viii) Economy. 
5.3 For guidance, Table 1 may be referred for selection 
of feeders based on material sizes. 


IS 14169 : 2013

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’.
